objective.text: Use BCC for a shared announcement when recipients must not see one another’s addresses.

difficulty.rationale: Choose delivery addressing that does not expose the full recipient list in message headers.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: A single generic announcement must reach several customers, but recipients must not see one another’s addresses in its headers. Which addressing choice supports that requirement?

options.text: Place customer addresses only in Reply-To.
options.rationale: Reply-To controls where replies go; it does not designate the intended delivery recipients.
options.misconception: Reply-To controls where replies go; it does not designate the intended delivery recipients.

options.text: Place the customer addresses in BCC, with a suitable public sender/To identity.
options.rationale: BCC recipients participate in delivery without their address list appearing in the transmitted message headers.

options.text: Place the customer addresses in CC.
options.rationale: CC addresses are visible in the message headers.
options.misconception: CC addresses are visible in the message headers.

options.text: Place every customer address in To.
options.rationale: To recipients can see the other To addresses.
options.misconception: To recipients can see the other To addresses.

explanation.summary: BCC recipients participate in delivery without their address list appearing in the transmitted message headers.
